source_records.title: Critical assessment of machine learning approaches for classification, dynamic prediction and surrogate modeling in food fermentation
source_records.license: Open access under a Creative Commons license; confirm exact article/supplement terms before reuse
source_records.results_context: Study-specific results: knowledge-based and ML dynamic-prediction comparisons use experimental time-series data; the approximately 0.6% surrogate result is fidelity to the knowledge-based model on synthetic test cases, not real-world fermentation measurement error.
source_records.use_gate: Reproduce the published data definitions, split strategy, uncertainty and baseline values first. Separate empirical NRMSE from synthetic simulator-fidelity error; compare on same inputs, targets and test units. Treat the hybrid residual network as a candidate, not a presumed winner.
claims_not_supported: universal superiority of mechanistic or ML models

source_records.title: Industrial baker's yeast fed-batch fermentation nutrient-addition time series
source_records.publisher: figshare deposit referenced by the public analysis repository

reported_reference_result.caveat: Numbers are reported in the public code companion; not independently reproduced. Per-batch errors vary materially, and only 10 full-process batches are in this result.
reported_reference_result.additional_caveat: Pooled MAPE of about 10.46% masks the B04 held-out batch MAPE of about 32.98%. Report batch-level distributions and worst-batch error rather than only pooled metrics.

source_records.use_gate: Verify the Figshare deposit's current license and metadata, download authorized files, record byte-level SHA-256 and column/units dictionary, audit missingness and unusual records, then reproduce the published leave-one-batch-out baseline before any comparison. Review each feature's actual timestamp/availability against the feed-decision cutoff; current-hour target/feature alignment may describe the historical operator policy rather than prospective controllable prediction.
claims_not_supported: beer, wine or spirits performance without separate domain validation
prospective feed-control benefit from current-hour feed-rate reconstruction
generalization beyond represented batches or strain
SOTA superiority without matching the published split, preprocessing and metrics
industrial resource saving or safe actuator control
source_records.next_benchmark: Compare persistence/last-action, simple regression, tree baseline and sequence models under identical leave-one-batch-out splits; separately score truly next-hour prediction after an explicit feature cutoff, calibration, error by batch, and matched decision value.

source_records.title: Effect of data availability on in-line adaptation of fermentation mechanistic models under abnormal conditions

reported_scope.method: Monod-type kinetics with empirical decay terms; posterior Bayesian parameter inference on truncated post-detection data; genetic-algorithm fitting as more data accumulate; phase-dependent switch

source_records.data_availability: Article states underlying data are confidential; the full industrial dataset is not a public reproducibility benchmark.
source_records.use_gate: Treat published numbers as study-specific literature comparators. Build synthetic contract tests from method structure only. Require an open/licensed independent dataset before empirical re-analysis; do not reconstruct private trajectories from figures without checking reuse terms.
source_records.benchmark_value: A reference for phase-aware estimation under different data availability regimes and model-process mismatch, not a beverage-specific baseline.
claims_not_supported: the same numeric improvement on a different process
contamination diagnosis accuracy without detection labels and protocol
causal production recovery, safer control, or feed-policy benefit
model superiority on the full industrial data
source_records.research_question: Can a predeclared model-switch policy choose a better-calibrated estimator as the available post-detection prefix grows, while preserving abstention and hard process constraints?

research_notes: Public process-related time-course data exist in research repositories; the gap is not absolute absence but fragmented formats, limited numbers of independent fermentation units, heterogeneous targets, and few standardized industrial sensor streams with aligned batch IDs and quality outcomes.
Primary intake candidate: Dryad 2026 CC0 wine-temperature/yeast-ecology files, after raw-byte and replicate-structure audit.
Separate curve-reproduction candidate: 2026 Frontiers wine-kinetics article and supplement; table/uncertainty reproduction is not external validation.
Transcriptome time courses are biological evidence, not direct process-sensor or final-quality targets.
Synthetic fermentation data are for pipeline and fault-injection tests only.

An additional industrial process-data candidate is a baker's-yeast fed-batch dataset (59 batches/1,090 hourly rows reported by its code companion). It is not alcoholic beverage data; use it as an external process-method validation only after the Figshare license and source bytes are verified.

Reported current-hour feed-rate prediction may not be a prospective control task unless all inputs are proven available before the target decision. Evaluate next-hour and decision-cutoff tasks separately.

Published 2026 abnormal-fermentation adaptation results use 30 confidential industrial contaminated runs. They motivate the evaluation protocol but cannot be independently reproduced from the cited dataset.

The novel open benchmark target is decision quality under truncated data and model mismatch: compare fixed estimators and a declared switch policy at each detection prefix, with calibration, abstention and constraint-violation metrics.
